Mutual funds are bought and redeemed at the unit price, so they have one price a day, with no high, low or volume. Max drawdown = the largest fall from a peak to a trough within the year, which measures the real risk an investor went through. Annual volatility measures how sharply the price moves.

Confidence combines the strength of the reasons for and against with the success rate of the same setup on this stock's own history. Below 55% means a weak signal.

The nearest support zone below the price: a level the price bounced from more than once. Buying in steps inside it is better than chasing the price.
The nearest resistance above the price: a level the price turned down from before. Suitable for taking profit or reducing the position.
The price at which you exit if the price breaks the buy zone, so the loss stays small and decided in advance.
How much you gain for each unit you risk. 1 : 2 means a possible gain twice the possible loss.
Measures the speed of the move from 0 to 100. Above 70 is overbought (rose fast), below 30 is oversold (fell fast).
Judged from where the price is relative to the long moving average and the direction of its slope.
Measures momentum as the difference between two exponential averages. Above the signal line is bullish momentum, below it bearish.
The difference between the stock's performance and the whole market's over the same period. Positive means the stock is stronger than the market.
Candlestick chart with support and resistance zones
Drag the chart to move, and use + and − or Ctrl with the mouse wheel to zoom.

Green zones are support and red zones are resistance; the more times the price touched them, the stronger they are. The “Volume” tag means heavy trading happened inside the zone, and the “Weekly” tag means it also shows on the weekly timeframe; both make it stronger.
Factors that move the gold price
A high gold-to-silver ratio means silver is relatively cheap. The dollar index usually moves opposite to gold. US Fed meetings cause big swings in gold.
The professional rule: don't risk more than 1% to 2% of your capital on a single trade. The calculator sets the number of shares so your loss stays within that if the stop loss is hit.
Success means reaching the target before the stop loss within 30 candles. Past results do not guarantee the future.
The test replays what the tool would have said on each past day using only the data available up to that day, then measures what happened next.
P/E = price ÷ annual earnings per share; lower means relatively cheaper than companies in the same sector. Dividend yield = annual dividends ÷ price.
Local peaks and troughs are detected, and those close in price are grouped into one zone whose width depends on the average true range.
A zone gets stronger with more and more recent touches, with the volume traded inside it, with showing on the weekly timeframe, and with switching between support and resistance.
A breakout counts as confirmed when the price closes clearly beyond the zone on volume at least 40% above normal and holds there.
Confidence combines the strength of the reasons with the historical success rate of the same setup on the same asset.
